newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED ON WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED ON WEDNESDAY.

text.p: HARARE, July 2 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer in quiet Wednesday trade, dealers said.

The market opened short of 155 million, but the central Reserve Bank, forecasting a Z$600 million surplus at the end of the day, sold 91-day treasury bills amounting to Z$400 million at a steady discount rate of 25 percent.
The central bank paper was being traded on the secondary market at 24.75 percent, unchanged from Tuesdy, but call money added one percentage point to 23 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.5 percent, up from 26 and sold at 25.5 from 25 percent while bankers acceptance bills were quoted at unchanged at 25.5 percent (buying) but firmer at 25 from 24.85 percent (selling).
